scoff.title: You and <neon>food</neon>
scoff.intro: Before we talk about weight, five short questions. It is not a diagnosis: it tells us whether to avoid deficits and weigh-ins.
scoff.question: Does any of this happen to you?

items.sick: Making yourself sick when uncomfortably full
items.control: Worry about losing control over how much you eat
items.fat: Feeling fat when others say you are thin
items.dominate: Food or weight dominating your thoughts or life
items.weightLoss: A recent large weight loss that worried you or others

scoff.followUp: Does it happen often, or does it bother you a fair amount?
scoff.followUpControl: Do you have episodes of eating a lot while feeling unable to stop?
scoff.incomplete: Answer all five questions to continue.
scoff.single: Noted. A single yes is not a positive screen; we will keep an eye on it.
scoff.positive: From your answers, FightLab will not suggest deficits, weight targets or weigh-ins.
scoff.redoNote: If things change or a professional reviews you, you can redo it from your profile.

basics.weightInvalid: Enter a valid weight in kg (30–250).

Breathlessness at rest or with mild effort

register.title: Create <neon>account</neon>

empty.bodyRange: Try a wider range or log a measurement.

trend.title: Trend weight
trend.info: The trend is a smoothed average of your weigh-ins: it ignores daily water and glycogen swings and shows where your weight is really heading. Trust the line, not the dot from today.
trend.toGoal: Trend is <hl>{n} kg</hl> from your goal ({goal} kg)
trend.atGoal: Trend is at your goal ✓ ({goal} kg)

bmi.label: BMI <hl>{n}</hl>
bmi.info: BMI = weight / height². General reference: 18.5–24.9 is considered "normal". Note: in athletes with muscle mass it overestimates body fat — use it only as a guide.

chart.needDistinctDays: Log measurements on different days to see the chart.
chart.needMore: Your chart will appear after a couple more measurements.

photos.title: Progress photos
photos.empty: Take a photo every now and then (same light, same pose) and you will see progress the scale does not show. Later on, AI will also be able to analyze them.

new.title: New <hl>measurement</hl>
new.subtitle: Weight is enough. The rest is optional.
new.girthsHint: Waist is the most useful one for seeing progress the scale does not show.

body_fat_pct.label: Body fat %
body_fat_pct.info: The percentage of your weight that is fat. If you do not know it, leave it blank. It is measured with bioimpedance scales or skinfold calipers.

resting_heart_rate.label: Resting HR
resting_heart_rate.info: Beats per minute at complete rest, ideally on waking and lying down. The lower it is, the better your cardiovascular fitness usually is.

hrv_ms.label: HRV
hrv_ms.info: Heart rate variability: how much the time between heartbeats varies. Higher = better recovery and less stress. Measured by watches and bands (Garmin, Whoop, Oura).

sports.title: Sports
sports.subtitle: Pick your activity, time it and track kcal.
sports.rpeInfo: RPE = Rating of Perceived Exertion (1-10 scale): how hard it felt. 1 = very easy, 10 = maximum effort (you couldn't do more).

live.wakeNote: The screen won't turn off during the session. If you close the app, you can pick it back up.

summary.title: How did it go?
summary.saveNoRpe: You can save without RPE, but with it we calculate your load.

activity.title: Your activity
activity.empty: You haven't logged any activity yet. Time a sport and it will show up here.

mma.rpeInfo: RPE = Rating of Perceived Exertion (1-10 scale): how hard the session feels. 1 = very easy, 10 = maximum effort (you can't do more).

hints.sparring: Live rounds. High RPE — control the intensity with your partner.
hints.drilling: Technique repetition with a partner, at low intensity. Quality over fatigue.
hints.pads: Mitts/pads: combinations at a medium-high pace with feedback from your coach.
hints.bag: Bag work: power, volume or cardio depending on the day.
hints.technique: Shadowboxing and form without opposition. Low RPE — precision.

plan.title: Suggested plan
plan.note: For now it's based only on the art and the type. Coming soon: <ai>AI-personalized</ai> from your history and your load.
plan.sparring: {art} · sparring {minutes}': split it into rounds (e.g. {rounds}×3' with 1' rest), start at 60% and build up. Finish with 5' easy.
plan.drilling: {art} · drilling {minutes}': pick 1-2 {kind, select, grappling {positions or transitions} other {combinations}} and repeat them cleanly in rounds, switching with your partner.
plan.pads: {art} · pads {minutes}': rounds on the mitts with called combinations; technique first, pace after.
plan.bag: {art} · bag work {minutes}': alternate technique rounds (precision) with power or pace rounds. Use the round timer in Tools.
plan.technique: {art} · technique {minutes}': shadow work in front of a mirror on guard, footwork and 2-3 specific movements. No rush.
plan.conditioning: {art} · conditioning {minutes}': specific intervals (jump rope, burpees, clinch, sprawls). Keep your form even when fatigue hits.

reminder.grappling: Short nails, keep your gi/rashguard clean and look after your elbows and knees.
reminder.strikingShins: Bring hand wraps, shin guards and a mouthguard; protect your wrists.
reminder.striking: Bring hand wraps and a mouthguard; protect your wrists.

reply.stretch: Finish with 5-8 min of gentle stretching (hips, hamstrings, shoulders, neck), 20-30 s each, no bouncing.
reply.warmup: Warm up for 8-10 min: mobility, jump rope or an easy jog, and progressive sets of today's technique. Don't go into sparring cold.
reply.hydration: Sip water throughout the session; at high intensity add electrolytes. Arrive already hydrated.

load.title: Load and status
load.subtitle: Calculated from your real sessions and measurements.
load.recoveryEmpty: Log resting HR and HRV for a few days in Biometrics and your recovery status will show up here.
load.acwrProvisional: Provisional: it calibrates until you have 4 weeks of history ({days}/28 days).
load.acwrNoRecent: No sessions in the last 7 days: your ACWR is back as soon as you log a workout.
load.acwrBuilding: Unlocks with ~10 days of sessions with RPE (you have {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}).
load.acwrEmpty: Log your workouts with RPE (Sports, MMA or Gym) and the ACWR will calculate itself.
load.weekEmpty: No sessions this week. Your workouts with RPE will show up here.
load.noVariation: No variation between days: alternate hard and easy
load.footer: Data from this device · it will move to your account with the sessions backend.

info.state: Your readiness to train today, based on your recovery signals (resting HR and HRV) compared with your own average.
info.acwr: Acute (7-day) to chronic (up to 28 days) load ratio. Between 0.8 and 1.3 = safe zone; above that, injury risk goes up. It needs history: it's marked provisional until you reach 4 weeks.
info.load: Load per session = duration × RPE (arbitrary units, AU). Your Sports, MMA and Gym sessions logged with RPE are added up here.
info.monotony: How similar your daily loads are (mean/deviation over the last 7 days). Very high = little variation, more risk; alternate hard and easy days.
info.strain: Strain = weekly load × monotony. It measures your total accumulated stress for the week.

cuidado.label: Take it easy
cuidado.phrase: Your recovery signals are below your average. Today: light technique or active rest.

listo.label: Ready to train
listo.phrase: Recovery above your average. A good day for hard work.

normal.label: Normal day
normal.phrase: Signals around your average. Train according to your plan.

briefing.care: Your recovery signals are low: today, easy technique or active rest comes first.
briefing.acwrHigh: Your load is rising too fast (ACWR {acwr}): cut the volume for a few days.
briefing.ready: Recovery above your average: a good day for a demanding session.
briefing.week: Week under way: {au} AU so far. Keep the pace and log every session.
briefing.unknown: I don't know you well yet: log your workouts (with RPE) and your measurements, and this briefing will become truly yours.
briefing.weigh: Weigh-in in {days} days and you're {over} kg over: gentle deficit, no aggressive cuts yet.

acwrHigh.title: Load rising fast (ACWR {acwr})
acwrHigh.why: Your week is well above your average. Add a technique or rest day to get back to the safe zone (0.8–1.3).

acwrLow.title: You have room (ACWR {acwr})
acwrLow.why: You're below your chronic average: you can push harder this week with no added risk.

recovery.title: Low recovery signals
recovery.why: {chips}. Prioritise 8 h of sleep; if tomorrow is the same, cut the volume.

weigh.title: {over} kg over target · weigh-in in {days} d
weigh.whyFar: Reasonable margin: keep the deficit and don't touch water or sodium yet.
weigh.whyNear: Not much time left: review the plan and check with your team before any aggressive cut.

oldWeight.title: No weigh-in for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
oldWeight.why: Weighing in every 1-2 weeks keeps your trend and your macros reliable.

start.title: Log your first session of the week
start.why: With your workouts (duration + RPE) I calculate your load and your ACWR, and warn you before you overdo it or fall short.

ok.title: No alerts: all good 👊
ok.whyData: Load in the safe zone and recovery on track. Stick to your plan and see you tomorrow.
ok.whyNoData: No alerts for now. The more workouts and measurements you log, the sharper I get.

chat.greeting: Hi. Ask me about your training, load, weight or recovery: I'll answer with your numbers.

reply.acwrPaused: ACWR on hold (no sessions in the last 7 days)
reply.acwrPending: ACWR not calculated yet (I need ~10 days of sessions)
reply.weightNone: I don't have your weight yet. Log it under Biometrics and I'll track the trend.
reply.weightOver: You're {over} kg from target with {days} days to go. Reasonable pace: moderate deficit and no water cuts until the last 48-72 h, and sensibly.
reply.weightAt: You're already at your target weight ({target} kg) with {days} days to go. Maintain and arrive fresh.
reply.weightLast: Your latest weight is {weight} kg. If you have a fight, set up the weigh-in under Nutrition and I'll handle the plan.
reply.hardCare: Today is not the day to kill yourself: {chips}. Quality technique (RPE 5-6) and get some sleep.
reply.hardHigh: Your {acwr} says you've had a sharp rise. My call: a technical session today and the hard one in 2 days.
reply.hardReady: Recovery above your average and {acwr}: go hard today, you have room. Warm up well.
reply.hardNormal: From what I see ({acwr}), a normal plan day. Log the session when you finish and I'll adjust the advice.
reply.fatigueNone: I don't have your recovery signals yet: log resting HR and HRV for a few days and I'll read them to you every morning.
reply.load: Week: {au} AU. {acwr}. Monotony {mono}. Safe zone: 0.8–1.3; avoid two spikes in a row.
reply.loadNone: No sessions this week yet. Log your workouts with RPE and I'll calculate load, ACWR and alerts.
reply.summary: Your snapshot today: {parts}. Want today's plan?
reply.summaryNone: I don't have any data on you yet. Start by logging a workout or your weight and we'll talk.
reply.thanks: Get to work. Log the session when you finish and I'll add it to your load. 🥊
reply.default: I'm listening. Ask me about today's training, your load, your weight or your recovery — I'll answer with your real numbers.

signs.title: Warning signs
signs.intro: Tick only what is happening. If you are unsure, read the description again; if it is still unclear, do not tick it and act on it as soon as it appears.
signs.cardiac: Chest, neck, jaw or arm pain or pressure, breathlessness, dizziness or fainting, or palpitations (during exercise or at rest)
signs.cardiacEmergency: It is chest pain at rest, fainting, or chest pain with breathlessness and sweating
signs.systemic_illness: Fever, aches all over, or feeling unwell below the neck
signs.head_cold: Just a head cold (runny nose or sore throat, no fever or aches)
signs.disordered_eating: Vomiting, laxatives or diet pills, exercising to make up for food, bingeing with loss of control, or a marked fear of gaining weight
signs.disorderedUrgent: Also: fainting, confusion, eating almost nothing for 2 days or more, or vomiting several times a day
signs.rhabdo: Very sore, weak or swollen muscles with dark urine after training
signs.injury: New pain or an injury in some area
signs.injurySevere: The pain is sharp or getting worse, or I have numbness or weakness

readiness.reduce: You have had 3 days of drops on 2 or more signals against your baseline: hold or reduce the load.
readiness.pragmatic: These thresholds are pragmatic, not validated: a guide, not a diagnosis.

weightTrend.okNow: Average of the last week: {kg} kg
weightTrend.okBasis: It compares the average of the first week with the last, never a single weigh-in.
weightTrend.insufficient: No trend yet. It needs at least {min_points} weigh-ins covering {min_days} days; you have {points} over {days} days.
weightTrend.empty: No weigh-ins yet. With 7 weigh-ins spread over 14 days you will see your trend.
weightTrend.blocked: Weight tracking is switched off for you.
weightTrend.chartNote: The chart line is visual only: a smoothed average of your weigh-ins. The weekly rate comes from the coach's trend.

bodyFat.hint: With DXA, BodPod, lab-grade BIA or skinfolds the coach can use your lean mass to estimate your energy use (Cunningham equation). With a smart scale or another method it cannot: the measurement error would go straight into the calculation.
bodyFat.blocked: With your current safety profile weight, body fat and girths are not saved; resting heart rate and HRV are.
